is_anopheles.evidence: The study evaluated Anopheles gambiae sensu stricto and Anopheles arabiensis (Page 3).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper mentions that the laboratory Kisumu-kdr strain has the L1014S (kdr-east) mutation, but no marker genotyping assays were performed as part of this study (Page 3).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No extractable genotype counts, allele counts, or genotype frequencies were reported.

african_field_population.evidence: The study exclusively tested five laboratory-reared colony strains (Kisumu, Kisumu-kdr, Ifakara, Mbita, Kingani) in a semi-field system in Bagamoyo, Tanzania (Page 3, Page 9).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical semi-field study evaluating transfluthrin eave-positioned targeted insecticide (EPTI) (Page 2-4).

sub_country_location.evidence: The semi-field experiments took place in Bagamoyo, Tanzania (Page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Experiments were carried out between March 2018 and September 2019 (Page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Primary empirical semi-field study using established insectary strains.

supplement.evidence: No supplementary data is needed because no field genotyping was performed.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the efficacy of transfluthrin eave-positioned targeted insecticide (EPTI) in reducing human landing rates of five laboratory-reared Anopheles gambiae s.s. and Anopheles arabiensis strains with varying levels of pyrethroid resistance inside a semi-field system in Bagamoyo, Tanzania. No field populations were collected or genotyped.
exclusion_reasons: The study only tested long-established laboratory mosquito colonies (Kisumu, Kisumu-kdr, Ifakara, Mbita, Kingani) rather than African field populations.
No extractable target marker genotyping data was generated or reported.
